What is this?

Write a regex. See it think.

Relay is an in-browser regular-expression playground. You type a pattern and some test text, and Relay highlights every match live, lists the capture groups, explains the pattern token by token in plain English, and draws an SVG railroad diagram of its structure. There's a replace/split workbench too. The whole thing runs client-side — open index.html over file:// and it just works.

What's inside

No regex library, no diagram library, no framework, no build step — everything is hand-written vanilla JavaScript.

Real matching

Matching uses the browser's native RegExp engine, with the d (indices) flag where available to resolve exact capture-group offsets — and a 250 ms guard against catastrophic backtracking.

A real parser

A hand-written recursive-descent parser turns your pattern into an abstract syntax tree — literals, classes, quantifiers, groups, lookaround, alternation, backreferences. The AST drives the explainer and the diagram.

Railroad diagrams

The diagram pane runs a two-pass SVG layout (measure, then draw) over the AST: sequences flow left-to-right, alternations stack and fan out, quantifiers draw loop-back rails, groups become labelled boxes.

Live overlay highlights

A transparent textarea sits over a synced overlay div; matches are <mark> spans in alternating colors, with capture groups tinted distinctly — handling overlaps, multiline text, and zero-width matches.

Replace & split

A transform workbench shows live String.replace output with $1, $<name>, and $& tokens, plus a split mode that lists every resulting part.

Shareable & persistent

Your pattern, flags, and text are saved to localStorage and encoded into the URL hash. Copy the share link and the whole session travels with it.

How a pattern flows through Relay

  1. 1
    Parse — parser.js reads the source string left to right, building an AST node for each construct and counting capture groups.
  2. 2
    Match — matcher.js compiles a real RegExp and iterates every match, resolving group offsets and bailing if a run blows past the time budget.
  3. 3
    Highlight — highlight.js turns matches into overlay spans, nesting capture-group tints and marking zero-width hits.
  4. 4
    Explain — explain.js walks the AST into an indented, plain-English breakdown.
  5. 5
    Draw — railroad.js lays out and renders the AST as an SVG railroad diagram.

Keyboard shortcuts

⌘/Ctrl + /Focus the pattern field
⌘/Ctrl + EnterRe-run matching
